sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Open-Market Brokerage of Solid-State Drives and Server Processors

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid bijural system: Quebec private and commercial matters are governed by the Civil Code of Quebec (RLRQ c CCQ-1991) and the Quebec Business Corporations Act (RLRQ c S-31.1); federal public, regulatory, AML and tax statutes operate within the Common Law tradition; corporate registration is administered by the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA; in force 1 Oct 2014)
Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA; in force 1 Jul 2020)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP; in force for Canada 30 Dec 2018)

Convention between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (DTA; in force 28 Dec 1986, as amended by 2016 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000 c 17, as amended, and its Regulations (PCMLTFA); Criminal Code, RSC 1985 c C-46 ss 462.3 and 462.31 (laundering offence); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985 c C-44 s 21.1 et seq (individuals with significant control register); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992 c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985 c U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), SC 2017 c 21; Export and Import Permits Act, RSC 1985 c E-19 (dual-use semiconductor export controls); Investment Canada Act, RSC 1985 c 28. Provincial: Loi sur les societes par actions, RLRQ c S-31.1 (QBCA) and Regulation; Loi sur la publicite legale des entreprises, RLRQ c P-44.1; Charte de la langue francaise, RLRQ c C-11; Loi sur la taxe de vente du Quebec, RLRQ c T-0.1; Code des professions, RLRQ c C-26 (notarial acts); FINTRAC interpretive guidance on politically exposed persons, suspicious transaction reporting and record keeping.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of UBO identity documents (passport, national identity card) and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or licensed chartered professional accountant (CPA) in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille - Canada acceded to the Apostille Convention effective 11 Jan 2024; apostille issued by the competent authority of the document's country of origin (e.g., PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Chinese-issued documents)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Existence / Certificate of Good Standing of corporate beneficial owners (where UBO is a legal person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the corporate UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via designated Competent Authority of the issuing jurisdiction; consular legalization only if issuing state is not party to the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation for SWIFT TT / escrow inspection wire provenance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Remitting bank or escrow agent holding the funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy authenticated by Hague Apostille where the letter is used outside the issuing bank's jurisdiction; otherwise bank-attested letter with legalized signature acceptable to Quebec counsel

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney authorizing Quebec incorporation agent and registered office service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary (for Quebec-origin POA) or notary in the principal's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the foreign-origin POA; Quebec notarized original for domestic use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / certified resolution of the beneficial owner appointing founding directors and initial officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporation counsel or CPA firm in Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by Quebec Minister of Justice or Global Affairs Canada if the certificate is destined for foreign bank or counterparty onboarding

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated List, the PCMLTFA Entities and Individuals Lists, Global Affairs Canada autonomous sanctions under SEMA, the OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists (required because payment rails are USD SWIFT TT / escrow wire), the Criminal Code terrorist entity list, and commercial PEP databases covering domestic PEPs (Canada), foreign PEPs and heads of international organizations within FINTRAC's expanded definitions. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier, including identification of source of funds, source of wealth, and a written explanation of the commercial purpose of spot semiconductor brokerage. Coroner-level review applies where a UBO is resident in or funds originate from high-risk jurisdictions; files must be retained for at least 5 years under PCMLTFA record-keeping rules. Dual-use screening under the Export and Import Permits Act and Wassenaar classification must be documented for server processors and high-performance SSDs prior to first shipment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) online filing service at www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca (primary provincial route); federal alternative for a CBCA corporation: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre at www.ic.gc.ca/ecd with extra-provincial registration in Quebec under the Loi sur la publicite legale des entreprises within 60 days of commencing business
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must comply with the Charte de la langue francaise: the distinctive element must be in French unless a linguistic authorization is obtained; the legal element must be a French designation or its recognized abbreviation such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Compagnie' or 'Ltee'; a NUANS search must be filed against the French-language name; the articles and all public filings are prepared in French (or bilingual), and transliteration into Latin script is mandatory for any foreign-language distinctive element; an English-only name triggers REQ refusal absent a certificate issued under the language charter.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chambre de commerce / Board of Trade
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: 1) Upon REQ refusal, prepare a fresh NUANS report and re-file within 30 days via the REQ online service with a corrected distinctive element or a linguistic justification letter under the Charte de la langue francaise; 2) submit a written administrative review request (demande de revision) to the Registraire general within 60 days of the refusal, annexing the original notice, the new NUANS report, and any trademark or trade-name opposition evidence; 3) if the administrative review is denied or not answered, seek judicial review before the Court of Quebec under the Code of Civil Procedure, RLRQ c C-25.01, arts 529 et seq, within 30 days of the final decision; 4) in parallel, reserve the rejected name federally under the CBCA if the corporate vehicle is switched to a federal corporation, or adopt a distinctive French sub-brand for Quebec commercial activity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible as registered office (siege social) under QBCA s 9 and the Loi sur la publicite legale des entreprises only where the address is a real, geolocatable physical street address in Quebec staffed by a person authorized to accept legal service; pure virtual mailboxes and PO boxes are rejected by REQ. For a spot semiconductor brokerage with USD wire rails, a virtual-only structure materially increases adverse bank onboarding outcomes; the entity should maintain verifiable books and records in Quebec, board minutes at the registered office, and at least one bank or escrow relationship with a Quebec-chartered financial institution to satisfy enhanced AML/CFT substance expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated combined annual likelihood of unannounced physical on-site inspection in the first operating year: approximately 12% (industry base rate 5% for Revenu Quebec and REQ verification activity; +3% incremental due to Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML classification; +2% for a virtual-office registered address; +2% for cross-border UBO and USD wire exposure). No mandatory on-site program exists for unlicensed wholesale distribution; inspections arise mainly through GST/QST registration audits, source deduction (CNESST) compliance reviews, or suspicious transaction referrals.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Accredited NUANS search house (private trustee under Corporations Canada/REQ protocol)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of CAD 45-50 plus taxes per report; mandated before filing articles

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of Articles of Incorporation under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (electronic filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff approximated at CAD 350 per REQ fee schedule, subject to annual indexation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration in the Quebec Enterprise Register (declaration d'immatriculation / legal publicity with NEQ number)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of approximately CAD 100 for legal person registration under the Loi sur la publicite legale des entreprises

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notification under the Investment Canada Act (establishment of a new Canadian business by non-Canadian UBO)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory filing fee; preparatory administrative benchmark for corporate counsel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional legal fees for corporate draftsmanship (articles, by-laws, organizational resolutions, optional unanimous shareholder agreement, bilingual French/English versions)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for boutique business law firms (CAD 1,200-1,800 estimated)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office (siege social) service - 12 months, Quebec physical address, legal service of process, mail forwarding
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate service provider or trust company in Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of approximately CAD 400 per annum

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified statement of registration and certificate of status (releve de l'entreprise / attestation de conformite) for bank and escrow onboarding
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee of approximately CAD 35-40 per certified extract

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Apostille bundle for UBO identity documents, POA, bank reference and incumbency certificates (approx 5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec notary / Quebec Minister of Justice (Apostille service) / Global Affairs Canada
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Combined notarial tariff (CAD 60-120 per act) plus CAD 15-30 per authentication/apostille under GAC and provincial fee schedules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register implementation and initial AML/KYC file (individuals with significant control register under QBCA, PEP and OFAC/UN/sanctions baseline screening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance consultant / CPA firm in Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of approximately CAD 550-650 for FINTRAC-ready KYC packages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GST/QST registration, payroll source deduction (CNESST) file setup and CRA/Revenu Quebec business number coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Revenu Quebec / Canada Revenue Agency (via licensed agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government registrations carry no fee; agent administrative benchmark of CAD 200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Regulatory classification memorandum and dual-use export screening manual (MSB registration applicability, EIPA/Wassenaar controls for SSD and server processors)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cross-border trade counsel / trade compliance specialist
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for discrete export control and FINTRAC classification opinions (CAD 650-750)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank and escrow KYB documentation pack for USD SWIFT TT and escrow inspection wire rails (completed corporate structure, UBO register extract, source of funds report)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of CAD 275 for bank-grade KYB dossiers

stage_2.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
stage_2.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 4 (services/wholesale without manufacturing); no EIA procedure under the Regulation respecting the environmental impact assessment and review procedure (REIE) applies
stage_2.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC discharge thresholds are applicable to a pure wholesale brokerage; if a storage facility is operated, waste packaging must be disposed of by an authorized municipal collector, and any accidental release of electronic components/pollutants must be declared under s. 70 of the Environmental Quality Act; Quebec e-waste recovery obligations under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products by enterprises may apply if the company trades regulated electronic equipment above exemption thresholds.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) through the Business Registration Online portal and My Business Account; for Quebec, Revenu Québec (RQ) through the Quebec Business Number (NEQ) and registre des entreprises du Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign corporation carrying on business in Canada or making taxable supplies in Quebec must first obtain a federal Business Number (BN) with a corporate income tax account via CRA Business Registration Online. If the corporation makes taxable supplies other than zero-rated supplies in Canada and is not a small supplier, it must open a GST/HST account under the same BN. For Quebec, the corporation must register with Revenu Québec for QST purposes, obtaining a Quebec Business Number (NEQ) and a QST account. Where the non-resident corporation has no physical presence in Quebec, registration may still be required based on solicitation, inventory, or deemed permanent establishment rules; a representative fiscale is commonly required for CRA and Revenu Québec communications.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not have a US-style check-the-box regime. A business corporation is always a separate taxpayer subject to entity-level federal and provincial income tax. Relevant elections include: (i) the section 216 ITA election permitting a non-resident to compute Canadian-source rental or timber royalties on a net basis; (ii) GST/HST related-party or joint venture elections; (iii) the small supplier election to accelerate GST/HST registration; and (iv) CRA-administered deemed-dividend rules for hybrid mismatch concerns. Quebec provincial tax classification follows the federal classification; no provincial check-the-box election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (5% federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) plus Quebec QST (9.975% Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies for GST/HST and QST small-supplier status; registration becomes mandatory once a person exceeds C$30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive quarters. Non-resident sellers may be required to register without the normal threshold where goods are drop-shipped or inventory is located in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently impose a real-time fiscal clearance, government pre-clearance API, or digital stamping mandate. CRA and Revenu Québec accept electronic invoices if they are complete, intelligible, and retained to support an audit. The Pan-Canadian Trust Framework and PEPPOL interoperability are voluntary standards for e-invoicing. There is no statutory requirement to obtain prior CRA or Revenu Québec validation of individual export invoices for zero-rating purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods qualify for 0% GST/HST and QST if the goods are exported by or on behalf of the supplier, transferred to a non-resident, and delivered outside Canada as part of a continuous chain of transportation. A supply of services to a non-resident is eligible for zero-rating under Schedule VI, section 7 of the Excise Tax Act unless it relates to real property in Canada, goods situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, or is performed wholly in Canada in relation to a person who is not a non-resident. For open-market wholesale trading of SSD and CPU chips, the seller must maintain an unbroken chain of transport documentation from the Canadian supply point to the foreign customer, including transit through bonded logistics if applicable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canadian Customs Export Declaration (B13A) or authorized customs broker export report
Commercial invoice with HS/ECC classification (HS 8471 for SSDs; HS 8542 for CPUs/processors)
Bill of Lading (ocean, air, rail, or truck CMR) or associated house/master airway bill
Packing list with part numbers, quantities, serial numbers, weights, and destination
Canadian International Trade Single Window / ACI eManifest cargo control document
Purchase order, sale contract, or non-resident buyer letter of credit evidencing the foreign customer
Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT MT103 wire confirmation matching the exported shipment value
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec cross-match export declarations with freight manifests, payment data, and corporate income tax filings. Missing or inconsistent export documentation causes the zero-rating to be denied and the full 14.975% output tax to be assessed, plus interest from the original return due date. False export claims with knowingly false statements attract penalties up to the greater of C$25,000 and 100% of the tax sought to be evaded, plus potential director liability, penalty assessments under section 285.1 of the Excise Tax Act, and a four-year normal reassessment period that is extended indefinitely where misrepresentation is established. Fines for wilful evasion can reach up to 200% of the evaded tax in egregious cases, and export refund claims are subject to enhanced audit scrutiny where the foreign buyer is related or payment is repatriated later than the contractual remittance deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Floating exchange rate regime with full convertibility for current account transactions including profit remittances following tax clearance. Capital account transactions generally require prior Bank of Canada approval for portfolio investments exceeding thresholds. Profit remittance subject to Canadian tax obligations and FINTRAC reporting only.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds required. All export receipts must be reported to FINTRAC if value exceeds CAD 10,000 for anti-money laundering compliance. No statutory conversion ratios or timelines apply.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited viability for offshore electronic money institutions due to Canadian Payment Services Regulations and AML requirements. Traditional correspondent banking through Tier-1 banks remains primary channel for cross-border corporate liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote KYC and video verification permitted for corporate onboarding. Directors may be required to attend physical interviews for transactions exceeding CAD 50,000 or elevated cross-border risk profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or export control screening hits on counterparties or jurisdictions involved in semiconductor trade
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-use certificates, validated export licenses, source-of-funds statements, beneficial ownership declarations, and transaction purpose codes

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent beneficial ownership structures or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry extracts, director and officer interviews, and enhanced due diligence reports

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires via SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. Beneficiary details must match corporate charter and KYC dossier. All transactions subject to FINTRAC reporting and beneficial ownership verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements routed via SWIFT MT103 for trade settlements or Commercial Letters of Credit for larger transactions. Purpose codes include 'Trade Payment' or 'Merchandise Payment'. Correspondent banking relationships established with international institutions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties and potential dissolution after two years of non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required only if the corporation is a distributing corporation or exceeds shareholder/asset thresholds under the Business Corporations Act (Quebec). Private corporations with 50 or fewer shareholders and not distributing shares are exempt.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation mandated; shareholding transfers do not require annual filings. Beneficial ownership data may be requested for regulatory purposes.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%). Federal rate derives from the 38% base less 10% provincial abatement less 13% General Rate Reduction.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 4651 wholesale brokerage. Effective levers: 13% General Rate Reduction (T2 Line 350); accelerated Capital Cost Allowance on computing and logistics equipment; SR&ED credits are immaterial to pure wholesale trading; the Small Business Deduction (federal 9% / Quebec 3.2% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income) is unavailable where the controlling shareholder is non-resident.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) filed electronically through CRA-certified e-file software (My Business Account or third-party ESD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual by fiscal year-end; quarterly instalments of Part I tax where the corporate tax liability exceeds CAD 3,000; Part XIII withholding remitted monthly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 due within 6 months of the fiscal year-end (December 31 year-end is due June 30). Final Part I balance due 2 months after year-end (3 months for an eligible CCPC claiming the Small Business Deduction); Part XIII WHT remitted by the 15th of the month following payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income for tax purposes computed under Part I of the Income Tax Act before loss utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide business income of the Canadian-resident corporation. For a Quebec wholesale subsidiary of a foreign parent, confirm the Quebec permanent establishment and do not substitute a foreign-head-office allocation absent factual profit attribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 4 and provincial abatement lines
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apportionment of taxable income among provinces plus the 10% federal provincial abatement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income to Quebec using gross revenue and payroll weights of the Quebec establishment. A foreign parent cannot direct an arbitrary override of the statutory allocation factors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General Rate Reduction: 13% of the lesser of taxable income allocated to a province and income not eligible for the Small Business Deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Wholesale gross margin is generally eligible; claim the reduction only on income allocated to Canadian provinces.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit claim and final federal tax payable after credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the federal foreign tax credit only for true foreign-source income and foreign taxes; a Canadian wholesale corporation cannot use an FTC to erase Part I tax on Canadian distribution income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: ITA s. 235: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeat-filing penalty 10% plus 2% monthly. Automatic late-filing penalty under ITA s. 162(1): CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500. Arrears interest compounds daily at the prescribed rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Revenu Quebec Form CO-17 (Corporation Income Tax Return) filed electronically via Revenu Quebec Efile-Entreprises.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual by the same fiscal year-end as the T2; instalments coordinated with federal instalment payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CO-17 due within 6 months of the fiscal year-end; Quebec balance of tax due 2 months after year-end (3 months for an eligible CCPC). Late instalments attract prescribed interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of federal taxable income to Quebec taxable income through Quebec tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A corporation resident in Quebec pays Quebec tax on business income allocated to Quebec; non-resident shareholders do not compute Quebec corporate tax on their own account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 11.5% Quebec general corporate rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No Quebec rate reduction or holiday exists for wholesale computer-component brokerage; compute the tax strictly on Quebec-allocated taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-capital loss carryforward and carryback application for Quebec purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quebec follows the 20-year carryforward / 3-year carryback of the federal non-capital loss regime; losses of a predecessor foreign entity cannot be used unless transferred under an amalgamation or winding-up.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Parallel late-filing penalties under the Quebec Taxation Act (5% plus 1% monthly up to 12 months); daily penalty for failure to file an information return; interest compounded daily at the Quebec prescribed rate; denial of the 10% federal abatement restoration not available until the Quebec return is filed.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder under Part XIII ITA (s. 212(2)); reduced by applicable tax treaty, commonly 5% where the beneficial owner is a company controlling at least 10% of the voting stock and 15% in portfolio cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Withhold the full 25% unless prior treaty relief is secured: (1) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's residence jurisdiction; (2) file CRA Form NR301 with the TRC before the dividend wire is released; (3) remit the reduced withholding under the confirmed treaty rate; (4) if over-withheld, the non-resident claims a refund through the Part XIII annual return or the federal T1/T2 refund process. Quebec imposes no separate provincial dividend WHT, but the dividend must be coded as 'dividend' in the Swift_TT remittance narrative and reported on an NR4 slip.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for trademarks, software and know-how: 25% statutory (ITA s. 212(1)(d)), reduced to 10% under most DTAs. Interest on shareholder and third-party debt: 25% statutory (ITA s. 212(1)(b)), reduced to 10% under most DTAs; participating-debt interest and thin-capitalized interest remain at 25% absent treaty relief. Excess interest on non-arm's length shareholder debt is non-deductible and may be recharacterized as a deemed dividend attracting full 25% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: T106 and RC4643 disclosures are mandatory where aggregate transactions between the Canadian wholesale corporation and each non-arm's length non-resident exceed CAD 1,000,000 per fiscal year. CRA records thresholds under TPM-09: CAD 5,000,000 for tangible goods, CAD 1,000,000 for loans, services and intangible property. A Local File is expected at these levels; a Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required when the multinational group consolidates revenue of at least CAD 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Quebec has no GCC-style Economic Substance Regulation filing. Substance is enforced through the GAAR (ITA s. 245), Quebec anti-avoidance provisions, CFC/FAPI attribution (ITA ss. 91-95), and the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test embedded in Canada's treaties. A Quebec shell with no staff, office, management, physical inventory, or commercial risk will lose treaty protection and be reassessed as a conduit. Demonstrated substance: local employees performing procurement and sales, title passage in Quebec, storage or inspection of SSD/CPU inventory in Canada, and locally maintained books and records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to record cash or wire sales of SSD/CPU inventory, issuing false supplier invoices, or routing rebates through a foreign affiliate to suppress Canadian taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax (ITA s. 163(2)). Criminal conviction under ITA s. 239: fine of 50%-200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years. Quebec parallel penalties under the Taxation Act. Reassessment window extends to 10 years for misrepresentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Quebec letterbox corporation that books wholesale profit while management, negotiation, inventory risk, and decision-making sit with a Hong Kong or BVI affiliate; claiming the 5% treaty dividend rate without value creation in Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and de facto directors exposed for counselling unremittance; personal assessments for the 25% WHT default; director disqualification; asset-seizure orders and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve false intercompany invoices may be jointly liable for the penalty and interest; criminal exposure for fraudulent manufacture of books; bar from directorship under corporate law upon fraud conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who control wire tables and fail to implement AML/CFT controls may be prosecuted personally; travel bans, asset freezes, civil restitution orders, and voidance of D&O insurance for intentional misconduct.
